definitions.explanation: The former Japanese academic title roughly equivalent to associate professor. Officially replaced by {准教授|じゅんきょうじゅ} in 2007, but still widely understood and occasionally used.

examples.japanese: ⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦かつて→かつて：10303_katsute⟧⟦{大学|だいがく}→大学：00608_daigaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{助教授|じょきょうじゅ}だった。
examples.english: My father was once an associate professor at a university.

examples.japanese: {助教授|じょきょうじゅ}⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{肩書|かたが}き→肩書き：13909_katagaki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{現在|げんざい}→現在：01556_genzai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{使|つか}われていない→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: The title of associate professor (jokyōju) is no longer used today.

examples.japanese: 2007⟦{年|ねん}→年：09876_nen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{助教授|じょきょうじゅ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{准教授|じゅんきょうじゅ}→准教授：19861_junkyouju⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{改|あらた}められた→改める：12923_aratameru⟧。
examples.english: In 2007, the title jokyōju was changed to junkyōju (associate professor).

notes:
Composed of {助|じょ} (assistant, helper) + ⟦{教授|きょうじゅ}→教授：02589_kyouju⟧ (professor). This was the standard title for the rank below full professor in Japanese universities until 2007, when the School Education Act was revised and the title was changed to ⟦{准教授|じゅんきょうじゅ}→准教授：19861_junkyouju⟧.

The change was made partly because {助|じょ} ("assistant") was seen as implying a subordinate role, whereas {准|じゅん} ("associate") better reflected the independent standing of the position.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{准教授|じゅんきょうじゅ}→准教授：19861_junkyouju⟧: associate professor (current official title)
- ⟦{教授|きょうじゅ}→教授：02589_kyouju⟧: professor
- ⟦{助教|じょきょう}→助教：27895_jokyou⟧: assistant professor (current title, created in the 2007 reform)
- ⟦{講師|こうし}→講師：00451_koushi⟧: lecturer

USAGE:
Still frequently encountered in older texts, historical accounts, and popular media. Many people continue to use {助教授|じょきょうじゅ} informally even after the official change.
